reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 09 and targeted source panel/note crops, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native face/collar and note crops, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png; checked the right-facing pose and slightly parted mouth, cap emblems, covered hair/sideburns, moustache versus beard, uniform/cross, collar fit, source two-row note footprint versus returned rows, and visible transparency.

remaining_reasons: The enlarged original note has TWO compact upper gray-mark rows and largely blank lower paper. The returned native note clearly has THREE distinct rows: two dark dashes on row one, two blurred groups on row two, and an additional lower third row of multiple gray marks. Remove the invented third row/extra gray clusters and restore only the source-scale two-row upper footprint without adding replacement marks.
entries.positive_observation: The dark olive peaked cap retains its shiny black visor, gold piping/cord, one upper gold eagle-shaped emblem and one lower gold wreath/cockade emblem. Covered hair with localized dark sideburns, dark eyebrows and one short dark upper-lip moustache remain without a chin/jaw beard or glasses. The three-quarter head and gaze face image right, and the slightly parted single mouth retains a small pale tooth edge. Upright shoulders, chest-up crop, strong visor shadow and warmer cheek/mouth light remain. The dark high-collared uniform retains one pale-edged dark cross at the throat. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk, pinching or clipping. The complete tilted frame, opaque muted warm grey-olive backplate, overlapping cream note and right-edge contour remain. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring; the added third note row is the separate visible rejection reason above.
entries.visible_limitations: The moustache/mouth pixels, fine cap embroidery and collar-cross detail are extremely small at 65x67 and are not additional rejection grounds. Note glyphs are not readable text, but the source-page crop clearly resolves two rows versus the returned three distinct rows, so the rejection does not depend on interpreting lettering or rejecting unresolved detail.
